A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison. The original appendices A–C are retained as C–E in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original English STS/MTEB evaluations, cross-lingual retrieval and STS results, ablations and embedding analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds multilingual-model evaluations, baseline embedding-norm comparisons and quantitative clustering analysis.

M1.justification: Appendix A adds a four-language variant that applies sentence-level PCA jointly across languages and explicitly skips embedding refinement. The original extraction procedure, bilingual and monolingual losses, sentence averaging and ensemble method remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The training corpora, evaluation datasets, tasks and four represented languages are retained. The multilingual experiment reuses English, German, Chinese and Japanese on existing retrieval/STS tasks; it changes the model configuration rather than task coverage.

E2.justification: The main benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged. Appendix B/Table 12 newly compares fastText, WordLlama and Model2Vec against OURS in the POS-based embedding-norm analysis; v1's corresponding analysis compared only stages of the proposed method.

E3.justification: The added multilingual comparison uses joint four-language PCA without fine-tuning, alongside retained fine-tuned bilingual models. Section 5.2 adds silhouette scores to the clustering evaluation, and Section 3.1 reports an extraction-sample comparison of N=30 versus N=100. Existing benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds checks of bilingual versus multilingual training and baseline POS-norm patterns, quantifies existing language-clustering visualizations, and reports qualitative sample-count and text-length sensitivity findings. These extend the retained component, teacher-model, PCA and model-size analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions average runtime over three independent runs in Table 2. v2 adds no seed information, confidence intervals, variability estimates or specified significance tests. The new silhouette scores measure clustering, not uncertainty.

E6.justification: The existing benchmark and ablation scores are retained. New multilingual retrieval averages are 93.1, 86.6 and 71.6 for en-de, en-zh and en-ja, compared with retained bilingual values of 95.7, 91.2 and 79.0 under different training conditions. v2 also adds multilingual STS results, baseline norms and silhouette scores of 0.10, 0.11 and 0.02.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 corrects the teacher/student assignment of T and S. Section 3.2 generalizes the PCA matrix to LM rows, but its explicit centering expression uses a length-M ones vector, introducing a dimensional inconsistency when L>1. The loss equations and ensemble identity otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion qualify the PCA claim from removing semantically irrelevant components to removing components with low semantic relevance. The main contributions remain intact; superiority over SimCSE on MTEB was already claimed in v1's introduction.

C2.justification: v2 acknowledges that bilingual training may favor OURS against multilingual comparators. It adds interpretations linking baseline POS norms to retrieval behavior and teacher pooling to distillation performance, and qualifies some causal wording. The existing word-order and long-context limitations remain, with document retrieval explicitly identified.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents BlingFire sentence splitting, short-sentence selection, Nomic's 'classification: ' prefix, teacher pooling and limited temperature tuning. These disclose settings without establishing changes to existing experiments. The release statement now promises code alongside models, still in future tense.

R1.justification: The cited-work list is unchanged. Section 2 removes the explicit criticism that WordLlama and Model2Vec have unclear tuning processes and lack embedding analyses, softening the paper's positioning against those projects.

P1.justification: v2 makes local prose corrections and expands explanations of refinement, preprocessing and ablations. Two appendix sections are inserted before the retained material, while the main section sequence and overall narrative remain stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 10–12, relocates existing figures and tables, and gives ensemble results a separate subtable with revised bolding in Table 13, formerly Table 10. All six existing figures retain their plotted content. These are incremental display and layout changes.

improvement.justification: The multilingual check, quantitative PCA support, baseline-norm analysis and implementation disclosures modestly improve evidential support and reproducibility. The gains have limits: the multilingual comparison also omits fine-tuning, and the expanded PCA notation introduces a local dimension error. Overall, the added clarity and supporting evidence outweigh these limited shortcomings.
